items.headline: Stocks fell again Tuesday; S&P 500 and Nasdaq notch a fourth straight loss
items.note: On Nov. 17 the S&P 500 fell 1.03% to 7,340.53, the Dow fell 1.64% to 50,759.42 and the Nasdaq fell 0.74% to 24,328.38. Worries about AI chip demand and AI disrupting software weighed on tech, and all 11 sectors ended lower.

items.headline: Nvidia beats analyst estimates in its first report since Jensen Huang's exit
items.note: Shares rose as much as 3% in after-hours trading, easing some worries about AI infrastructure demand. I couldn't confirm the exact revenue and guidance figures, so check Nvidia's release. Its results set the tone for AI spending and hiring.

items.headline: Anthropic likely to price its IPO above the $70–$78 range
items.note: CNBC's sources say the order book closed at 4 p.m. ET Tuesday, with trading as ANT on Nasdaq slated for Nov. 19. Pricing hadn't been confirmed when I checked. It's a big test of public appetite for AI labs.

items.headline: Anthropic's filing shows huge growth alongside a large paper loss
items.note: For the nine months to Sept. 30 it reported $33.24 billion in revenue, up roughly 1,200% from a year earlier, and a $104 billion net loss that the company attributes mostly to fair-value changes on convertible notes and derivatives. Worth reading as a case study in how to read an S-1.

items.headline: Salesforce drops 9.45% as AI-replacement fears hit software stocks
items.note: Security concerns and fears that AI could replace software products drove the drop, and software and services were among Tuesday's weakest groups. It shows how fast investors reprice companies when AI changes the outlook.

items.headline: New U.S. limits on foreign access to advanced AI chips remain a worry for investors
items.note: Investors are still weighing the new restrictions, along with a run of tech outages that hit airlines and banks. Chip export policy can move AI stocks and affects where AI compute gets built.

items.headline: Tech layoffs keep climbing, but data roles are holding up better
items.note: Trackers put 2026 tech cuts at well over 140,000, with totals varying by method. Indeed's data and analytics postings index was above its level a year earlier while overall tech postings are far below their peak. Build concrete projects with statistics and ML for 2027 internships.

learn.term: Book-building (how an IPO gets its price)
learn.explain: Before an IPO, the banks running it collect orders from big investors at different prices. This list of orders is the 'order book.' If investors want far more shares than are offered, the company can set a higher price, which is why Anthropic is expected to price above its $70–$78 range. Once the book closes, the final price is set, usually the night before trading starts. Heavy demand often lifts the stock on day one, but it's no guarantee.
